description:
Jonah's Colony Manager
Automatic Colony Management, the mod.

Source code and guides
Required mods: none
Updating: delete the old Jonah's Colony Manager folder in mods/ and extract the new one. Safe mid-save, your settings stay with the save. MagicLib (Version Checker is built in) or TriOS tells you when there's a new version.
Safe to add mid-game

Breaks saves if removed

No known mod conflicts

Short summary
Flip a colony to Auto and it runs itself. It builds and upgrades within a budget you control, places your colony items and AI cores, hires administrators, handles policies, defends itself and deals with colony crises, across every colony you own. It plays by the game's rules: nothing is free, everything costs what it would cost you, plus a small convenience fee you can change.
Long description
This is a mod I had Claude Code create for me due to always liking to have tons of colonies with lots of buildings, limits off, etc, but always getting way in over my head with management.

The goal of the mod is to let you simply flick the automatic switch on your colonies and have them take care of themselves, so long as you have the cash to keep them improving. There's a Colony Autopilot button right on the colony screen (or right click Population & Infrastructure, it's the bottom option). There's several modes to choose from, tons of options involving governors, buildings, how you want the colony to develop, and so on!

By default, most of the settings will try to optimize your colonies to protect them and make them profitable, for a small convenience fee per building placed and action taken. To have it add items to your colonies, there is a colony storage you can access at any of your owned colonies where you can put all colony augment items (nanoforges, AI cores, etc.) - this has extensive modded support as well, and it'll ship things between colonies where they're needed for a fee and some travel time. I highly suggest going through the options to your taste, and they're editable on the fly from the Colony Autopilot tab in the intel screen.

The default will be on advisor so if you go into the settings nothing will be happening by default. If you switch it to approve or auto, the colony manager will get to work. I do recommend using approve or advisor unless you really just want to go completely hands-off. I play my playthroughs on auto currently. Sometimes I find it is a little bit better to tailor your initial colony specifically to what you're trying to do but that's what the presets are there for primarily. Just let me know if there are issues with them or if you have any problems.

I'm also currently working on progressing out a version that is more of a story version. You'll be working towards unlocking all the different functionalities of this mod slowly through getting AI cores and turning them in to either "fund" or "power" the functionality of the mod. That's still very early and I'm not ready to release that yet.

Features
Builds and upgrades on its own
Within a budget you control, following a plan worked out for each planet. Every building is weighed by what it adds to your share of each good's market across the sector, so your colonies spread out over different goods instead of all making ore. It never goes over a colony's industry limit, fixes one that ends up over, and never leaves a colony sitting at 0 stability (where the game can decivilize it). Items, AI cores and administrators
Drop colony items and AI cores into Autopilot Storage at any colony and it puts them where they do the most, shipping them over for a fee and travel time. Keeps colonies under the Hegemony's inspection radar, and hires and places administrators.
Low profile
If you'd rather not deal with colony crises, it keeps growing but stays under the radar: no AI cores above size 3, nothing that brings a Pather cell, no free ports, raids or sabotage. Each rule lifts once that faction's crisis is over for good. Guide Your capital
One colony becomes your home port: custom production and the loot in your other Storage tabs end up there, and once you're making money it turns into a trade hub with whatever buy/sell buildings your mods have.
Stations and stable locations
Every colony gets a station once it's past its first money push, and bigger ones as it grows. Comm relays, nav buoys and sensor arrays go up at your stable locations with a paid construction crew. Threats and colony crises
Plans for security when a colony is in danger, only builds defenses during a siege, and prices colony crises into everything it builds.
Surplus and the endgame
Spends big surpluses instead of letting money pile up, and once you're making a stupid amount a month it stops caring about money and builds for production, research and military instead. War, with Nexerelin
Defense and relief fleets, pirate base strikes, hitting back at whoever raids you, and agents on security, relations and sabotage. It never invades anyone.
Research, terraforming and more
Runs research, terraforming, trade contracts and megastructures when the mods for them are installed. Optional storage logistics ships refit gear to one station and known blueprints to another for selling. Plays fair
Doesn't change any balance and doesn't cheat for you. It manages colonies the way you would, pays convenience fees (configurable in options) and waits out travel time for administrators, agents, items and so on.
Talks like the colony AI it is
Everything it does pops up on screen as a short line with a code in front, like BUILD / Hot Springs: Planetary Shield (750k). The log keeps the full sentences, and there's a Plain setting if you'd rather have those on screen. Settings
Colony Autopilot button on the colony screen (or right click Population & Infrastructure), and the Colony Autopilot tab in the intel screen. Modes are Advisor (default), Approve and Auto, with goals like Balanced, Money, Security, War production, Rapid growth and Self-sufficiency. Every setting
Mod integrations
Works with 20+ colony mods: Nexerelin, Ashes of the Domain, Terraforming Made Easy, Industrial Evolution, Random Assortment of Things, Station Augments, Emergent Threats and more. None are required. Full list in the Supported mods spoiler below. Checkable
There's an audit page listing everything it can change in your game and what each thing costs, if you want to check it's safe first.

Getting started
Open a colony and hit the Colony Autopilot button.
Pick a goal (Balanced, Money, Security, War production, Rapid growth, Self-sufficiency) or leave it on Balanced.
Set the mode to Auto. The first time, it opens setup with recommended settings filled in. Just save it.
Drop any colony items and AI cores you want it to use into Autopilot Storage at any of your colonies.

Be warned: dropping this into your save and turning on Auto for all your colonies means they get autopiloted right away. It will start building things and doing stuff, which you may not immediately want. Put it on Advisor or Approve first to see what it wants to do, or back up your save, though it will tend to do things that are "correct".
Guides: getting started | how it builds | money and the endgame | war and security | items and cores | what it does with each mod

Supported mods
All optional, each one turns on by itself when its mod is enabled.
Terraforming Made Easy: special-world plans (Forge, Fortress, Paradise, Hive, Death, Waste) and terraforming, Domain-era upgrades for comm relays, nav buoys and sensor arrays
Forum thread
Industrial Evolution: ambassadors, edicts, VPC chips, specialized mining and refining, courier shipping
Forum thread
Nexerelin: defense, relief and war fleets (never invasions), agents, sieges, the Derelict Empire start
Forum thread
Ashes of the Domain (Vaults of Knowledge, Theory of Toolbox, Building Menu Overhaul): research, research locks, synergies, management styles, trade contracts, production orders, special projects, megastructures, wonders and gates, Hypershunt Receivers
Ashes of the Domain (Vaults of Knowledge, Theory of Toolbox) | Building Menu Overhaul
Emergent Threats (IX Revival): Antimatter Stabilizer conversion, Panopticon cores into the Surveillance Center
Forum thread
Random Assortment of Things: Frontiers settlement
Forum thread
Station Augments: best augment loadout per station, the Mining Station augment, economic in well-defended systems
Forum thread
Interstellar Imperium and Knights of Ludd: their stations count like vanilla ones, plus the Imperium station line
Interstellar Imperium | Knights of Ludd
Terraforming & Station Construction (Boggled): its terraforming projects and the buildings they need, mining and siphon stations founded as new colonies (optional)
Forum thread
Grand.Colonies: builds past 12 buildings, with the extra upkeep counted
Forum thread
Substance.Abuse: Breweries and recipes
Forum thread
Volkov Industrial Conglomerate: viral contamination treatment first, soil nanites only on vanilla farmland
Forum thread
Roider Union: Dives and Union HQ valued by what they mine nearby beyond what the colony already makes, Roider Charters placed
Forum thread
Planetary Shield: Access Control: the shield valued as defense, port kept closed with Pather cells
Forum thread
Unknown Skies, What We Left Behind, Astral Ascension: their mining conditions and water worlds, planetless colonies kept safe
Unknown Skies | What We Left Behind | Astral Ascension
Omega Core Everywhere and Astral Ascension Renewed: Omega cores go where they do the most, in a building or as an administrator
Omega Core Everywhere | Astral Ascension Renewed
Niko's Scavengable Industries: builds the blueprints you know, the risky ones are left to you
Forum thread
Junk Yard Dogs and Carter's Freetraders: resource forges and the Biolab, with illegal goods counted right
Junk Yard Dogs | Carter's Freetraders
Vulpoids: Organ Farms, the Biotech Facility, its colony items and Profecto administrators (the Vulpoid Bioforge story is left to you)
Forum thread
Yunru Industries, Yunru's Worlds and Slightly Better Tech-Mining: Secondary Drydocks, Auxiliary Shipbays, richer Tech-Mining
Yunru's mod thread (all three)
United Aurora Federation: its colony items placed by what they actually do
Forum thread
Jonah's Auto Outfitting: plans producers for the goods its big weapon orders need
GitHub
Any other mod: its deposits and colony items through the game's own tables, and its buildings measured on a test colony
Cloning (Oddisz): the three cloning industries built when faster growth is worth it, with room for the stability penalty to grow
Forum thread
Reverse Engineered Private Arsenal (Oddisz): left to you; never built or taken down, its core and Drone Replicator never moved
Forum thread
Sol Renewed (Oddisz): industries in Sol priced for what they add to its crisis meter, meter on the Crises page
Forum thread
Toolbox Economy Curves and Coalesced Little Mods (Oddisz): the curve you pick is planned with as is; the pack gets the same handling as Cloning and the Private Arsenal
Forum thread | GitHub

Checked and fine as they are, nothing needed: Better Colonies, Supply Forging, LOST_SECTOR, Kon's Player Faction Bundles, Galactic Constellate, Tri-Tachyon Expansion, Luddic Enhancement, Hillock, Hazard Mining, Hiver Swarm, Adversary, Gambling Den, Extra System Reloaded - Oddisz Edition, Hullmods - Renewed, Intel Renewed, StopBloatingMe, StopStackingMe, StarterPack, Discord Rich Presence.
If you would like one added please let me know here or in the GitHub issues and I'll do it asap.

Compatibility and permissions
Compatibility and known issues
Optional integrations: Nexerelin, Ashes of the Domain, Terraforming Made Easy, Industrial Evolution, Random Assortment of Things, Station Augments, Emergent Threats and a bunch more (Supported mods, above)
Tested with: my own 90-ish mod list, and every release is checked offline against every combination of the supported mods
Known conflicts: none that I know of, tell me if you find one
Known issues: expect bugs. This one's a lot deeper than it looks. Report them here or as GitHub issues with starsector-core/starsector.log and saves/common/colony_autopilot_diagnostics.json.data if you're up for digging logs, otherwise it's chill to just throw it in anyway. Your modlist helps a lot. Permissions
Code: use it however you want. Modpacks, reuploads, forks, copying the whole thing, building on it, all fine, no need to ask or credit me. Just don't sell it.
Assets: there's no art in the mod, same terms for everything

FAQ
Will it mess with my save if I add it mid-game?
It's safe to add, and it starts on Advisor, so nothing happens until you switch a colony to Approve or Auto. Removing it isn't safe: the Autopilot Storage tab lives on your markets.

Does it cheat?
No. Everything costs what it would cost you, plus a convenience fee you can change in options, and things like shipping items or hiring administrators take travel time.

I don't want colony crises. Can it avoid them?
Mostly. Pick Low profile when you found your first colony, or switch it any time under Settings, Expansion style. Pirates and the Persean League come from colony size alone, so nothing avoids those, but it gets you ready for them.

It isn't building anything. Why?
Check the mode (Advisor only advises) and the budget. The getting started guide has a section on exactly this.

Will you add more?
Yep, I'm updating it constantly, and if you want a mod supported, ask here or on GitHub and I'll do it asap. There's also a story version in the works.

AI use disclaimer
Some or all assets and code in this mod were created using AI tools:
Code: Claude Opus 5.5 (through Claude Code)
Docs, patch notes and the offline build checks: Claude Opus 5.5

No additional training data. There's no art in the mod. I came up with what it should do and tested it in my own games; the AI wrote the code and checks it offline against every combination of the supported mods before each release.

Made by Jonah's Tools | More: Jonah's Auto Outfitting | all my mods on GitHub

Thanks for playing!
